instruction: Bold the title text on slide 3 of the presentation.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to slide 2, selected the title text, opened font color picker and Character dialog, attempted to change color but set to Dark Gray 3 instead of black. Then moved to slide 3 and slide 4. Spent 50 turns without completing the multi-step task.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between slides in LibreOffice Impress, select text in title shapes, open font color picker and Character dialog, interact with text boxes
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to set the correct black color (chose Dark Gray 3 instead), could not bold titles correctly, and could not delete shapes/icons on slide 4. The original task was too complex with 3 sub-tasks across multiple slides.
metadata.task_rationale: Isolated the bold formatting sub-task on a single slide. The model demonstrated ability to select text and access formatting tools, so a focused bold-only task is a reasonable simplification.
metadata.explanation: Task requires bolding the title text on slide 3 (0-based index 2). The title 'Add an Agenda Page' has the largest font. Getter checks the bold property of all runs in the title shape. Metric verifies all runs are bold.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets slide 3 (0-based index 2) matching the instruction.
Title detection via largest font size heuristic is valid for this slide where 'Add an Agenda Page' has the largest font.
Getter correctly collects bold property from all runs and returns all_bold flag using strict 'is True' check, which properly handles None (inherited) values.
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly (expected.get('expected_bold')) consistent with type='rule' framework behavior.
Postconfig saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring state freshness.
Complete instruction coverage: single requirement (bold title on slide 3) is fully verified.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider using slide.placeholders to find the title placeholder instead of the largest-font heuristic, for more robust title detection in general cases.
